title: Nginx Reverse Proxy Security Hardening Blueprint for 2026
subtitle: Production guide for hardening Nginx reverse proxies with TLS 1.3, rate limiting, buffer overflow defense, and security headers.
hero_caption: Production Nginx Security Configuration Blueprint for Cloud Instances
exec_summary: Disable Nginx Server Tokens: Suppress server version disclosure in HTTP headers.
Buffer Overflow Defense: Restrict client_body_buffer_size and client_max_body_size.
Rate Limiting: Implement limit_req_zone to mitigate HTTP flood attacks.
TLS 1.3 Strict Ciphers: Mandate ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and modern TLS protocols.

content_paragraphs: By default, Nginx broadcasts its exact version number in HTTP response headers and 40x/50x error pages (e.g., Server: nginx/1.24.0). Attackers use this version information to query public CVE databases for unpatched vulnerabilities.
Suppressing server tokens is the first step in reducing information leakage across public endpoints:

sections.h2_title: 2. Mitigating HTTP Floods via Rate Limiting Zones
content_paragraphs: Layer 7 HTTP flood attacks attempt to exhaust Nginx worker connections. Configuring rate-limiting zones using limit_req_zone enforces request thresholds per IP address:

faqs.question: What is the difference between limit_req and limit_conn in Nginx?
faqs.answer: limit_req limits the rate of incoming HTTP requests per second, while limit_conn limits the total number of simultaneous active TCP connections per IP.
